summary.title: Powers of Ideals and the Cohomology of Stalks and Fibers of Morphisms
summary.executive_summary: This paper provides a short proof of a refinement of a theorem by Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog, and Trung regarding the regularity of powers of ideals. The central result establishes that for a positively graded Noetherian algebra, the limit of the end of the local cohomology of powers of an ideal, adjusted by the degree, exists and is related to the regularity of the stalks of a specific morphism. This result implies a conjecture by Huy Tai Ha concerning the a*-invariant and generalizes a result by Eisenbud and Harris for ideals primary for the graded maximal ideal. The author introduces the notion of regularity over a scheme to unify these results. A key contribution is the comparison between the cohomology of stalks and the cohomology of fibers of a projective morphism. The paper shows that for families of projective schemes that are close to being flat (where Hilbert polynomials of fibers differ by at most a constant), the maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree. This provides a geometric criterion for the linearity of the regularity of saturation of powers of ideals. Specifically, the limit of the regularity of the saturation of powers minus the linear term is non-negative if and only if the projection from the closure of the graph of the map defined by the generators to its image admits a fiber of positive dimension. The work also addresses the case where the morphism is finite, showing that the regularity of stalks and fibers coincide. The paper concludes with a collection of results covering the cases of finite morphisms and those with fibers of bounded dimension, providing a comprehensive framework for understanding the asymptotic behavior of regularity in powers of ideals.

Executive Summary
This paper provides a short proof of a refinement of a theorem by Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog, and Trung regarding the regularity of powers of ideals. The central result establishes that for a positively graded Noetherian algebra, the limit of the end of the local cohomology of powers of an ideal, adjusted by the degree, exists and is related to the regularity of the stalks of a specific morphism. This result implies a conjecture by Huy Tai Ha concerning the a*-invariant and generalizes a result by Eisenbud and Harris for ideals primary for the graded maximal ideal. The author introduces the notion of regularity over a scheme to unify these results. A key contribution is the comparison between the cohomology of stalks and the cohomology of fibers of a projective morphism. The paper shows that for families of projective schemes that are close to being flat (where Hilbert polynomials of fibers differ by at most a constant), the maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree. This provides a geometric criterion for the linearity of the regularity of saturation of powers of ideals. Specifically, the limit of the regularity of the saturation of powers minus the linear term is non-negative if and only if the projection from the closure of the graph of the map defined by the generators to its image admits a fiber of positive dimension. The work also addresses the case where the morphism is finite, showing that the regularity of stalks and fibers coincide. The paper concludes with a collection of results covering the cases of finite morphisms and those with fibers of bounded dimension, providing a comprehensive framework for understanding the asymptotic behavior of regularity in powers of ideals.

Research Context
An important result of Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog and Trung states that the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the power It of an ideal over a standard graded algebra is eventually a linear function in t. The leading term of this function has been determined by Kodiyalam in his proof. This result was first obtained for standard graded algebras over a field, and later extended by Trung and Wang to standard graded algebras over a Noetherian ring. More recently, Eisenbud and Harris proved that in the case of standard graded algebra A over a field, for a graded ideal which is A+-primary and generated in a single degree, the constant term in the linear function is the maximum of the regularity of the fibers of the morphism defined by a set of minimal generators. In a recent preprint, Huy Tai Ha generalized this result by proving that, if an ideal is generated in a single degree d, a variant of the regularity (the a*-invariant) satisfies a*(It) = dt + a for t >> 0. He conjectures that a similar result holds for the regularity.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether the limit of the end of the local cohomology of powers of an ideal, adjusted by the degree, exists and what it equals. The hypothesis is that this limit is at least equal to the initial degree of M for some i. The paper aims to prove a conjecture of Ha that a similar result holds for the regularity, not just the a*-invariant. It is hypothesized that for ideals generated in a single degree, the limit is the maximum of the end degree of the i-th local cohomology of the stalks of the projection. The study also investigates the relationship between the cohomology of stalks and the cohomology of the fibers of a projective morphism. It is predicted that for families of projective schemes close to being flat, the maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree.

Methodological Details
The study considers a positively graded Noetherian algebra A, a finitely generated graded A-module M, and a graded A-ideal I. The parameter d is defined as the minimum mu such that there exists p where (I^<=mu)IpM = Ip+1M. The proof utilizes the Rees algebra construction, setting RJ and RI as direct sums of powers of J and I. A bigraded onto map from S to RJ is constructed, where S is a polynomial ring over A0 with specific variable degrees. The equality of graded A-modules Hi_S+(MRI)(*,t) = Hi_A+(MRI)(*,t) is used to relate the cohomology of the Rees module to the cohomology of the powers. The finiteness of the cohomology modules is established using Theorem 2.1, which states that ai(M) is in {-infinity} union Z and the S0-module is finitely generated. The limit is analyzed by considering the support of the cohomology modules over the base ring B. The paper introduces the notion of regularity over a scheme, generalizing the usual notion of regularity with reference to a polynomial extension of a ring. The geometric setup involves the closure of the graph of the rational map defined by the generators of the ideal.

Procedures And Architectures
The proof of Theorem 4.1 involves writing J = (g1, ..., gs) and defining the Rees algebras RJ and RI. A bigraded map from S to RJ is defined by sending Ti to gi. The module MRI is shown to be a finitely generated bigraded S-module. The cohomology Hi_S+(MRI)(mu,t) is identified with Hi_A+(MIt)(mu+td). The limit of ai(MIt) - td is determined by the support of the cohomology modules over the base ring. Proposition 5.1 refines Theorem 4.1 by considering a graded ideal J subset I such that JIpM = Ip+1M. The limit is shown to be the maximum of ai(MRI tensor B' B'_q) over q in Proj(B'). Theorem 5.3 applies Proposition 5.1 to the case where I is generated by m+1 forms of degree d. The geometric interpretation involves the projection pi from the closure of the graph Gamma to the closure of the image W.

Key Results
The limit of (end(Hi_A+(ItM)) + i - td) exists for any i and is at least equal to the initial degree of M for some i. The limit of (ai(It) - dt) is equal to ai(Gamma), where Gamma is the closure of the graph of the rational map. The limit of (reg((It)sat) - dt) exists and is non-negative if and only if the projection pi admits a fiber of positive dimension. For a finite morphism, the regularity of stalks and the regularity of fibers are the same. If the Hilbert polynomial of any two fibers differ at most by a constant, the maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree. In the case where pi is finite, reg(It) = freg(Gamma) + td for t >> 0. If A is standard graded and reduced, and pi has fibers of dimension one, reg(It) = freg(Gamma) + td for t >> 0.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The result implies a conjecture of Ha on the regularity of powers of ideals. It generalizes a result of Eisenbud and Harris concerning the case of ideals primary for the graded maximal ideal. The comparison between cohomology of stalks and fibers provides a geometric criterion for the linearity of regularity of saturation. The notion of regularity over a scheme unifies the treatment of local and global properties of the ideal powers. The results cover the cases of finite morphisms and those with fibers of bounded dimension.

Contradictions And Limitations
The existence of the limit does not imply that all functions ai(t) are eventually linear functions of t. It only implies that at least one of them is eventually linear in t. The paper notes that for morphisms that are not finite or flat, the situation is more subtle. The results on the agreement of maximum regularities require the Hilbert polynomials of fibers to differ by at most a constant.

Claims
The limit of the end of the local cohomology of powers of an ideal, adjusted by the degree, exists and is related to the regularity of the stalks. The limit exists for any i. The limit is at least equal to the initial degree of M for some i. The existence of the limit does not imply that all functions ai(t) are eventually linear. This result implies a conjecture of Ha.
The maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree for families of projective schemes close to being flat. The maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree. For morphisms that are not finite or flat, the situation is more subtle. This provides a geometric criterion for the linearity of regularity of saturation.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The paper provides a short proof of a refinement of a theorem of Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog and Trung. The results are generalized to standard graded algebras over a Noetherian ring.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a short proof of a refinement of the regularity of powers of ideals, implying a conjecture of Ha. 2. The strongest evidence is the comparison between the cohomology of stalks and fibers, showing their agreement under certain conditions. 3. The future path involves extending these results to more general morphisms and algebras.
